object_description: orthogonal campus of varied volumes around a central esplanade
design_condition: The new volumes extend the existing development pattern around a common center, with an esplanade following the slope and a low gymnasium partly recessed into the terrain to connect naturally to the sports facilities.

positive.statement: The rectangular building volumes create attractive spaces that open to the neighborhood and connect the school complex with the district.
The independent orthogonal pattern establishes a common center and a precise formal and structural relationship between the parts.
The floor staggering of the existing building is elegantly incorporated into the access typology.
The central skylight illuminates the lightweight building and accentuates the roof area visible from the esplanade.
The open-plan access floor skilfully combines entrance, foyer, gallery and auditorium into an attractive group of public spaces.
The kindergarten proposal offers a child-friendly building structure with varied teaching methods and play options.
The spatial integration of the kindergarten works, and later conversion of its rooms into workrooms seems possible.
The new school draws its identity from a carefully implemented campus idea and develops practical use groupings within clear building structures.

negative.statement: The tree grove is not yet positioned in a sufficiently powerful and spatially precise manner relative to the building volume.
The open-space approach with extensive green cover remains tentative in its formulation.
The height difference between the school buildings and gymnasium obscures the obviousness of the access solution.
The requirements for protection, rescue and obstacle-free passage remain insufficient.
The positioning and topographical embedding of the grass playing field are not convincing and require major earth movements.
The barrier-free access at street level is unfortunate and highlights the general accessibility problem caused by the staggered floors.
The location of the textile-work rooms disrupts the desired spatial relationships within a teaching unit.
The route from the gym entrance to the cloakrooms and sports rooms uses a somewhat awkward staircase.
The reduced entrance hall, combined with mixed age groups, seems cramped.
The common center cannot match the intended generosity, and proximity between buildings creates a spatial bottleneck along the esplanade.
The carefully worked-out proposal still shows small weaknesses in terms of phasing.
